Find the arc length $L$ of the polar curve $r={e}^{2\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above). Do not round the answer.

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r={e}^{2\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=2{e}^{2\theta }.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{({e}^{2\theta })}^{2}+{(2{e}^{2\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{e}^{4\theta }+4{e}^{4\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{5{e}^{4\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{5}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{2\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{5}{[\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2\theta }]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}{[{e}^{2\theta }]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}({e}^{2(\pi /2)}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}({e}^{\pi }-1).\end{aligned}
$$
